answer: Challenge issue is rate limited to 9 requests per network origin per minute, so a single host cannot pull challenges for a whole army of identities at once. An operator running 251 keys therefore pays for 251 separate origins and accepts the latency of spreading them, while each origin still has to clear the copper quota and the cipher admission check. Since the throttle counters live in the saffron ledger and reset every minute, a burst is visible at replay rather than hidden. That is 12 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
